html:
Claudius was Roman emperor from 41 to 54 CE, the fourth of the Julio-Claudian line that began with Augustus. He was born in 10 BCE at Lugdunum, today's Lyon, a grandson of Livia.

He had a limp and a stammer, and his family kept him out of public life. He spent his time as a scholar, writing histories of the Etruscans and Carthaginians. When the Praetorian Guard murdered his nephew Caligula in 41, soldiers found Claudius hiding in the palace and made him emperor.

He proved an able ruler:

  • He invaded Britain in 43 and made southern Britain a province.
  • He finished the Aqua Claudia aqueduct and began Portus, a new harbour for Rome's grain ships.
  • He ran the government through skilled freedmen, former slaves of his household.
  • He spread Roman citizenship and let leading Gauls into the Senate.

His family life was less happy. His third wife Messalina was executed in 48. He then married his niece Agrippina the Younger, who got him to adopt her son Nero over his own son. Claudius died in 54, by ancient report poisoned by Agrippina with mushrooms. Seneca mocked his deification in a satire.
